New partnership gives Florida CPAs a way to earn required CPE credit through story-driven podcasts on topics from auditing to business transformation

TORONTO, Oct. 22, 2026 /CNW/ -- LumiQ, an audio-first continuing professional education (CPE) platform, today announced a partnership with the Florida Institute of CPAs (FICPA), giving Florida CPAs the ability to purchase curated podcast learning paths that count toward their required CPE. FICPA members can now purchase LumiQ's CPE podcast learning paths directly through the FICPA, with an initial set of 10 learning paths covering topics from auditing and taxation to business development and real-world business case studies.

The partnership makes the FICPA, which represents more than 20,000 members across Florida, the first state CPA society to offer its members this model of podcast-based CPE through LumiQ. It reflects the FICPA's ongoing effort to give Florida CPAs more flexible and engaging ways to meet their requirements.

Shelly Weir, President & CEO of the Florida Institute of CPAs, said, "The FICPA continues to search for solutions that both modernize CPE and uphold the standards of the profession. With podcasts having already reshaped the media and education landscape, our partnership with LumiQ will provide a new, engaging option for earning CPE that meets our members where they are."

Each CPE podcast learning path is a curated set of episodes built around a single topic. Members access their learning paths through LumiQ's platform or mobile app, allowing them to complete their CPE from anywhere and on their own schedule. The initial set of 10 includes Audit Nightmares, which examines real-world audit failures and the lessons behind them; Business Transformation in Practice, which explores how organizations like LEGO and Kodak navigated major turning points; and Tax Foundations: Individual, Estate, and Trust, which covers the basics of individual and estate tax planning. The full list of learning paths is available on LumiQ's website.

Joel Lessem, CEO of LumiQ, said, "We're excited to bring these podcast learning paths to FICPA's members. Each one lets CPAs dive deep on a single topic, from single audits to real-world business transformation case studies, so they walk away with practical knowledge that keeps them future-ready as the profession evolves."

FICPA members can purchase LumiQ's learning paths through FICPA.org.

About LumiQ

LumiQ is an audio-first CPE platform for accounting and finance professionals that turns required learning into strategic upskilling. Its podcasts are developed to be enjoyed and retained, giving professionals the knowledge and confidence to grow their careers.

About the Florida Institute of CPAs

The FICPA is Florida's premier professional association, serving more than 20,000 CPAs, corporate finance professionals, educators and students through advocacy, education, networking and leadership development opportunities.

Hosted by Meridian President & CEO Jay-Ann Gilfoy, the new season brings together entrepreneurs and leaders from across Ontario's small business ecosystem

TORONTO, Oct. 22, 2026 /CNW/ -- Meridian Credit Union is launching Season 3 of its Small Business Big Impact Podcast, returning with a new video-first format and a broader look at the people, partnerships and ideas helping small businesses succeed.

Hosted by Meridian President & CEO Jay-Ann Gilfoy, Season 3 moves beyond the traditional podcast format with in-studio video conversations designed to bring viewers closer to the entrepreneurs, advocates and community leaders shaping the future of small business.

"Small businesses are incredibly resilient, but no entrepreneur builds a successful business alone," said Jay-Ann Gilfoy, President & CEO, Meridian Credit Union. "Behind every business is an ecosystem of people, advice, partnerships and community support that helps turn an idea into something sustainable. This season is about having honest conversations with some of the people who are helping create those conditions and sharing insights that small business owners can actually use."

The Small Business, Big Impact Podcast is designed for entrepreneurs, founders, gig workers and those building, growing or supporting small businesses, with conversations grounded in the real opportunities and challenges business owners face.

Season 3 brings together voices from across the small business ecosystem to explore the ideas and issues shaping entrepreneurship today, from financial confidence and workforce development to advocacy, leadership, community impact and inclusive economic growth.

"Small business owners are navigating a lot, and they need more than financing," said Gilfoy. "They need people who understand their ambitions, trusted advice, strong networks and partners who are invested in their success. That's the bigger conversation we want to have with Small Business Big Impact."

Season 3 launches on October 22 with new episodes following monthly through March 2027. For the first time, audiences will be able to watch full episodes on YouTube in addition to listening through major podcast platforms, including Apple, Spotify, and Amazon.

The new season features a diverse lineup of entrepreneurs, business leaders and changemakers, including:

  • Rhiannon Rosalind, Founder and CEO, Conscious Economics – exploring how mindset, values and resilience shape entrepreneurship and what it takes to build a financially healthy business that reflects what matters to you.
  • Marc Soberano, Founder and Co-Executive Director, Building Up – discussing skilled trades, workforce development and how creating access to opportunities can strengthen businesses and communities.
  • Daniel Tisch, President and CEO, Ontario Chamber of Commerce – discussing the environment facing Ontario entrepreneurs, business confidence and the role of advocacy and partnership in supporting growth.
  • Roger Mooking, Celebrity Chef, Restaurateur, Artist and Host of Breaking Bread – exploring how entrepreneurship, culture and creativity can come together to build businesses that make an impact.
  • Emily O'Brien, Founder, Comeback Snacks – sharing how resilience, resourcefulness and bold thinking can turn adversity into an opportunity to build something new.
  • Pauline Caballero, Co-Founder, Power Yoga Canada – discussing the role of purpose and community in building a brand that connects with people and creates lasting relationships.

Watch the Season 3 trailer and catch the latest episodes of the Small Business Big Impact Podcast, featuring candid conversations with entrepreneurs and business leaders from across Ontario, on Meridian's website.

About Meridian Credit Union

Meridian is Ontario's largest credit union, and one of the largest in Canada. Guided by our purpose, "helping you achieve your best life," Meridian delivers personal, and wealth financial business solutions to over 390,000 Members. Our Meridian for Good strategy is aimed at helping people get access to the money and advice they need; plan for a better future that is clean, resilient, and diverse; and be financially confident. Meridian has one operating subsidiary: Meridian OneCap Credit Corp ("MOCC"). For more information, please visit: meridiancu.ca.

We also recognize the ancestral and unceded territories of all First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples across Turtle Island. ST. LOUIS, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Parents as Teachers National Center announced today that it has been named as a Finalist in two categories: Podcast Show in Content & Media, Education, Art & Culture and Podcast Episode in Content & Media, Health, in The 6th Annual Anthem Awards.

Anthem Winners are selected by the International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences. Judges for the 6th Annual Anthem Awards include an esteemed panel of leaders from leading organizations and companies dedicated to social impact, including Nancy Brown, CEO, American Heart Association, Heather Malenshek, CMO, Land O'Lakes, Inc., Jesse Tyler Ferguson, Award-Winning Actor & LGBTQ+ Advocate, Patrice Duckworth, Chief Inclusion Officer, Johnson & Johnson, Fatima Graves, President & CEO, National Women's Law Center, Justina Nixon-Saintil, Vice President & Global Chief Impact Officer, IBM, and many others.

"We're thrilled to see the impact sector bounce back, share their stories, and expand their impact after a challenging year last year," said Anthem Awards General Manager, Patricia McLoughlin. "This year's Finalists are truly setting the standard for how to advocate for a cause, inspire action, create impact, and overall make this world a better place."

The Parents as Teachers Podcast highlights experts and practitioners in the field of early childhood home visiting to share insight about supporting families during a child's earliest years. The show offers perspectives from diverse backgrounds to inform and enhance awareness across topics including early relational health, maternal and infant health, social support, and more.

Featured guests include leaders and professionals from Columbia University, Washington University in St. Louis, the Institute for the Advancement of Family Support Professionals, and more. The episode, recognized as a finalist, highlights the voices of a Parents as Teachers parent educator and mother, Christy Roberts, alongside her son, Will, an artist and speaker who is autistic.

"Every family has a story, and every voice has the power to inspire change," said Constance Gully, President and CEO of Parents as Teachers National Center. "Our podcast amplifies the voices and experiences of those working alongside families every day, sparking important conversations about early childhood development, maternal health, and family well-being. We believe these conversations have the power to inspire change and help every child get the strong start they deserve, and it's an honor to receive this recognition from the Anthem Awards."

Alongside the Finalist Announcement comes the launch of Anthem Community Voice in Partnership with NationBuilder, an annual voting campaign and celebration to uplift the work of Anthem Finalists. Supporters can celebrate the work of the Parents as Teachers Podcast online from October 13th to October 29th at celebrate.anthemawards.com. All Finalists are also in the running to win a Gold, Silver, or Bronze Anthem Award selected by Anthem judges. All Winners for the 6th Annual Anthem Awards will be announced on November 5, 2026.

About Parents as Teachers:

Parents as Teachers creates strong communities, thriving families, and children who are healthy, safe, and learning by matching parents and caregivers with trained professionals for regular personal home visits during a child's earliest years, from pregnancy through kindergarten. With over 188,000 families served in all 50 U.S. states, 127 Tribal organizations, and six other countries, the Parents as Teachers evidence-based home visiting model is backed by over 40 years of research-proven outcomes for children and families. Annually, Parents as Teachers National Center supports over 10,000 professionals and partners with more than 2,000 organizations, including school systems, social service nonprofits, health departments, tribal organizations, and military installations.

About The Anthem Awards:

Launched in 2021 by The Webby Awards, The Anthem Awards recognizes impactful brands, nonprofits, and individuals that are setting the standard for good worldwide. The Anthem Awards honors work across seven core causes: Belonging & Inclusion; Education, Art & Culture; Health; Human & Civil Rights; Humanitarian Action & Services; Sustainability, Environment & Climate; and Technology. This season's partners and sponsors include NationBuilder, Sustainable Brands, NationSwell, The Bloom, the Social Innovation Summit and The Nonprofit Alliance. The Awards were founded in partnership with the Ad Council, Born This Way Foundation, Feeding America, GLAAD, Mozilla, NAACP, NRDC, WWF, and XQ.

About The Webby Awards:

Hailed as the "Internet's highest honor" by The New York Times, The Webby Awards is the leading international awards organization honoring excellence on the Internet, including Websites and Mobile Sites; Video & Film; Advertising, Media & PR; Apps, Software & Immersive; Social; Podcasts; Games; Creators and AI. Established in 1996, The Webby Awards received over 13,000 entries from all 50 states and over 70 countries worldwide this year. The Webby Awards are presented by the International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences (IADAS). Sponsors and Partners of The Webby Awards include Adobe, WP Engine, Patreon, ElevenLabs, Framer, Meta, NAACP, KPMG, The Wall Street Journal, Deadline, The Hollywood Reporter, SXSW, The Podcast Show, and Authentic.

releases.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shawn Ryan, former Navy SEAL and host of "The Shawn Ryan Show," has partnered with the SIG SAUER Charitable Foundation to donate essential firearms and equipment to the Hickman County Sheriff's Department. Ryan and the SIG Team presented the donation in person yesterday alongside local county sheriff's deputies, the mayor, and city council members.

Driven by a mission to support law enforcement, Ryan acted after learning the department was facing severe budget constraints and utilizing equipment over 25 years old.

"How are these men and women supposed to protect our community if they're not properly equipped?" said Ryan. "As a Tennessee resident, I knew I needed to step in and help support our local community."

"When Shawn brought the Hickman County Sheriff's Department to our attention, we knew we had to help," said Jason Wright, VP of Marketing at SIG SAUER. "This initiative aligns perfectly with the SIG SAUER Charitable Foundation's mission, and we are proud to partner with Shawn to make it happen."

The donation equips the department with 30 SIG SAUER M400 rifles, ROMEO5 electro-optics, SLX suppressors, and FOXTROT-MSR compact mounted lights. Additionally, the department will receive top-of-the-line emergency kits to ensure officers are prepared for critical situations. At the event, SIG SAUER announced they will provide advanced rifle training for the department as well.

To learn more about Shawn Ryan, visit his podcast at shawnryanshow.com and follow him on social media. Additional information on the SIG SAUER Charitable Foundation is available at sigsauer.com.

For media inquiries or to schedule an interview, please contact Cathy Cardenas at cathy@cathycardenas.com.

Hosted by CEO Robert Dalton, the podcast brings professional insight, personal stories, and meaningful conversations to families navigating aging and homecare.

PEEKSKILL, N.Y., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What does it truly mean to age well? How can families prepare for changing care needs without sacrificing independence, dignity, or quality of life?

These questions drive the return of Embracing Angels, an educational podcast hosted by Robert Dalton, CEO of Angels on Call Homecare, an award-winning New York homecare organization specializing in Dementia, Parkinson's disease, and personalized aging-in-place services.

Originally introduced in 2024 with a focus on end-of-life experiences, Embracing Angels returns with an expanded mission: making conversations about aging, caregiving, and long-term care more accessible, informed, and meaningful.

"Over the years, I've seen how overwhelming it can be for families to navigate care decisions, especially when they don't know what questions to ask or where to turn," said Robert Dalton, CEO and podcast host. "I want this podcast to be a place where we talk openly about aging, share what we've learned, and help people feel better prepared for whatever comes next. These are conversations every family deserves to have."

Real Conversations. Diverse Voices. Meaningful Perspectives.

Embracing Angels explores subjects extending beyond traditional healthcare discussions, including aging in place, family caregiving, private-pay homecare, Dementia, Parkinson's disease, independence, and the emotional realities of supporting loved ones through life's transitions.

Through professional perspectives, personal narratives, and thoughtful discussions, the podcast seeks to connect healthcare expertise with lived experiences, offering listeners practical knowledge alongside stories that reflect the humanity behind care.

The relaunch episode, "Why We're Still Embracing Angels, and Private Pay Home Care Explained," addresses misconceptions surrounding homecare coverage and helps families understand important considerations when exploring care options.

Its return during Long-Term Care Planning Month reinforces the importance of education and proactive decision-making.

Extending a Legacy Beyond the Home

Founded in 2005 by Registered Nurse Pamela Fitzpatrick, Angels on Call Homecare has spent more than two decades advancing personalized homecare. Its distinction as the nation's first dual-accredited homecare provider in Dementia and Parkinson's care reflects its commitment to specialized education, clinical excellence, and meaningful quality of life.

"Redefining the aging experience requires more than advancing how care is delivered. It requires transforming how society understands aging itself," said Eric J. Dalton, Vice President of Angels on Call Homecare. "Knowledge creates confidence, and confidence empowers families to make decisions that reflect what matters most. Embracing Angels extends our belief that aging should never mean losing your identity, purpose, or voice. The conversations we start today can meaningfully shape the care people experience tomorrow."

Join the Conversation

Designed for older adults, families, Care Professionals, and healthcare professionals, Embracing Angels invites listeners to discover meaningful perspectives on aging, care, and human connection.

Founded in 2005, Angels on Call Homecare is a family-owned, New York State-licensed homecare provider serving eight counties throughout the Hudson Valley and Greater New York. Specializing in Dementia, Parkinson's disease, live-in care, and personalized aging-in-place services, the organization combines clinical expertise with relationship-centered support.

MIAMI, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The New Normal, the show about how enterprises are deploying AI agents and generating real ROI, today released its 13th episode and confirmed a weekly cadence through 2027. Presented by OutRival, the Miami-based company building AI digital workers for voice, SMS and email, the show has recorded 30 episodes with the leaders of some of the largest organizations in higher education, travel and government, and plans to have 100 recorded by 2027. New episodes publish every Thursday at thenewnormal.fm.

The New Normal is hosted by OutRival Co-Founder and CEO Ruben Harris and Co-Founder and President Timur Meyster. Vice President, Head of Travel Jeff Herzfeld, a 20-year cruise and hospitality sales operations veteran, co-hosts the travel episodes. The show's next chapter is insurance: recordings with carrier, agency and brokerage leaders begin Q4 2026, co-hosted by OutRival's Vice President, Head of Insurance, Eric Weinstein.

The Premise

Most AI coverage is about what might happen. The New Normal is about what already did. Every episode puts a senior operator in the chair to walk through the use cases they actually deployed, the numbers they actually saw, and the decisions they got wrong along the way. No vendor pitch, no futurism, just leaders who run large organizations explaining how the work is changing inside them.

How the Show Is Made

Every episode is recorded in person. The OutRival team gives each guest two options: fly to OutRival's headquarters in Miami, or the hosts fly to the guest's headquarters. The second option is the one the team prefers, because being on site is how you learn how a leader is actually thinking about these decisions, and it puts a light on the people behind the C-suite: the enrollment counselors, advisors, sales associates, contact center teams and technologists responsible for creating an amazing experience for every student, traveler and policyholder. The episodes are produced by Mike Landsberg and Thomas Risavy of Grove Station Studios.

The show was built for industries that live on the phone: higher education, insurance and travel, where the relationship between a brand and the people it serves runs through millions of calls, texts and emails. Nobody proves the point like Bob Becker, the cruise industry sales legend responsible for more than $50 billion in sales at Carnival, Norwegian and Celebrity, who filled ships primarily through the phone.

His episode, released today, is live here. Those are the industries where getting AI right matters most, because a human will always be in the loop at some point to create a delightful experience for the student, the traveler or the policyholder. The leaders on the show have already made the hard calls about where that point is, and they are thinking past the first call: how AI agents can help their people provide care through the entire journey, from the first inquiry to the trip after this one. Together, the institutions represented in the first 13 episodes serve more than one million students a year and millions of travelers.

Why the Show Exists

Every new normal begins as the risk most people avoid today and the standard everyone copies tomorrow. After conversations with more than 300 enterprise leaders, the OutRival team found that most companies are still not running AI in production at scale, and the few that are have a lead the rest of the market cannot see coming. The New Normal exists to put those leaders on the record. The guests are the ones putting digital workers on the org chart, writing job descriptions for them, and reorganizing teams so humans and AI work side by side.

Most companies still treat AI as reactive support, a smarter way to answer the phone once a customer finally calls. The leaders on the show flipped it. They use it to reach out first: the inquiry that never got a callback, the application someone almost finished, the policy up for renewal, the guest ready to book the next trip. The show covers inbound and back-office use cases too, but the questions it keeps coming back to are about where leaders stopped waiting and started the conversation themselves.

13 Episodes, Three Industries, One Format

The show launched in June 2026 with higher education, added the U.S. Department of Labor as its first government guest, and opened its travel chapter in October. Published episodes, in order:

  1. Kermit Cook, CEO, Penn Foster: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/penn-foster-kermit-cook
  2. Madeline Pumariega, President, Miami Dade College: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/miami-dade-college-president-madeline-pumariega-on-deploying-ai-at-scale-in-higher-education
  3. Scott Pulsipher, President, Western Governors University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/wgu-scott-pulsipher
  4. David Andrews, Chancellor, UMass Global: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/umass-global-david-andrews
  5. Mark Milliron, President, National University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/national-university-mark-milliron
  6. Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President, Southern New Hampshire University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/snhu-lisa-marsh-ryerson
  7. Gregory Fowler, President, University of Maryland Global Campus: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/umgc-gregory-fowler
  8. Taylor Stockton, Chief Innovation Officer, U.S. Department of Labor: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/dol-taylor-stockton
  9. Raghu Krishnaiah, Chief Operating Officer, University of Phoenix: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/university-of-phoenix-raghu-krishnaiah
  10. Justin Lonon, Chancellor, Dallas College: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/dallas-college-justin-lonon
  11. Mike Flaskey, President and COO, Marriott Vacations Worldwide: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/marriott-vacations-worldwide-mike-flaskey
  12. Dondra Ritzenthaler, CEO, Azamara Cruises: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/azamara-cruises-dondra-ritzenthaler
  13. Bob Becker, the King of Outbound, former sales executive at Carnival, Norwegian and Celebrity, released today: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/bob-becker-king-of-outbound

Insurance episodes, co-hosted by Eric Weinstein, will cover how carriers, agencies and brokers are putting AI agents to work. Additional higher education, travel and insurance executives are already recorded and scheduled.

What the Guests Are Saying

"I want more of our people to be able to do the heart work, and I want to offload the hand work," said Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President of Southern New Hampshire University, on where AI belongs at a university serving 300,000 learners.

"A pilot is an initiative. Scale is a transformation," said Madeline Pumariega, President of Miami Dade College, on why the college went all in rather than piloting.

"You don't have the reach that these digital workers do," said Mike Flaskey, President and COO of Marriott Vacations Worldwide, on what AI adds to a 1,400-person sales organization.

"So if AI's coming and it can help us, let's go," said Dondra Ritzenthaler, CEO of Azamara Cruises.

"Hope is a pretty poor strategy in business," said Bob Becker, the sales leader who built the outbound model used across the cruise industry, on why he started AI with one use case.

What the Hosts Are Saying

"The most useful conversations about AI were happening in private, between operators, and nobody was recording them," said Ruben Harris, Co-Founder and CEO of OutRival. "Thirteen episodes in, the pattern is clear. The leaders winning with AI did not wait for a perfect pilot. They put it to work on the conversations they were already having with students, travelers and policyholders, and they measured it. We have 30 of those stories recorded, and we will have 100 by 2027."

"Every enterprise is being told to deploy AI. Almost nobody is being shown what it looks like when it works," said Timur Meyster, Co-Founder and President of OutRival. "We built OutRival to put digital workers into production at scale, so we know the difference between a demo and a deployment. The New Normal exists to make that difference public. The leaders on this show are not forecasting. They are reporting results, and they are putting their names on them."

"I started on the phones at Carnival and spent twenty years running sales floors, so I know how this industry reacts to a pitch about the future. We've heard it. We've bought it. Launching October 15, the series brings together education leaders, researchers, school operators, students, and families to explore how demographic shifts affect school finances and academic opportunities, and what communities can do to prepare for a smaller future.

The series also addresses a critical question facing school leaders and districts: how to protect and build upon academic progress while simultaneously reshaping school systems for a smaller student population.

The first episode, "The Last Miss Douglass," premieres October 15, with new episodes released monthly on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, and other platforms.

"The Future Is Smaller" is produced by Jenny Dubin and Laura Hawkins. Associate Producers are Jason Rhein and Taylor Jackson. Sound design is by George Ingmire, and production management is by Elephant Quilt Productions. The podcast is sponsored by New Schools for New Orleans, with special thanks to Dana Peterson and Tiffany Delcour.

Listen and subscribe: https://rss.com/podcasts/the-future-is-smaller/

A National Challenge New Orleans Is Already Navigating

The number of school-age children is declining in communities across the country, driven by falling birth rates, population shifts, migration, and other demographic changes. For school systems largely funded based on student enrollment, those shifts can have significant consequences. In New Orleans, those pressures are already visible.

Over the past five years, K–8 enrollment has declined approximately 9%, while ninth-grade enrollment in 2026 is approximately 11% lower than in 2022. Meanwhile, New Orleans recorded its fifth consecutive year of academic growth on Louisiana's state assessments in 2026, improving three percentage points in students achieving Mastery or above.

The podcast builds on NSNO's longstanding work to help New Orleans public schools plan for a more sustainable system. Since 2022, NSNO has published regular analyses of enrollment, school capacity, and financial trends, helping school leaders, policymakers, and the public understand how demographic shifts are affecting schools today and what they could mean for the future. Through research and advocacy, NSNO has encouraged long-term planning that protects strong schools and directs limited resources toward students and educators.

New Schools for New Orleans is a nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to excellent public education. For 20 years, the organization has supported New Orleans schools through investments in educators, research, advocacy, and school sustainability. Learn more at www.nsno.org.

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Celiac disease has never had a platform — or a voice — quite like this.

The Celiac Disease Foundation has announced the launch of Inside Celiac, a new signature podcast hosted by acclaimed actress Katie Lowes, known to millions for her standout roles in Scandal, Inventing Anna, and The Hunting Wives. Drawing on her extraordinary ability to connect with audiences and her deeply personal experience living with celiac disease, Lowes will lead candid conversations that bring greater national attention to this serious, often-overlooked autoimmune condition.

Each episode of Inside Celiac will bring together leading medical and nutrition experts, patients, advocates, researchers, and other influential voices to explore what it truly means to live with celiac disease. Topics will include the often-long road to diagnosis, the everyday realities of maintaining a strict gluten-free diet, emotional health, family life, pediatric celiac disease, long-term medical care, groundbreaking research, clinical trials, and the urgent search for treatments beyond the diet.

"Living with celiac disease affects so much more than what is on your plate. It shapes how you travel, celebrate, work, parent, and move through the world," said Lowes. "I am thrilled to host Inside Celiac and create a space where people can hear honest stories, learn from trusted experts, and feel less alone. This series is about giving our community a stronger voice while helping the broader public understand the very real impact of this disease."

Celiac disease is a serious genetic autoimmune disorder in which ingestion of gluten causes damage to the small intestine and can lead to significant short-and long-term health consequences. Its symptoms can vary widely, contributing to delayed and missed diagnoses. While a strict gluten-free diet is currently the only treatment, maintaining the diet can be medically, socially, emotionally, and financially burdensome.

"Inside Celiac represents a significant new chapter in how we educate, engage, and advocate for the celiac disease community," said Marilyn G. Geller, chief executive officer of the Celiac Disease Foundation. "By pairing Katie's recognizable voice and powerful storytelling with the Foundation's trusted expertise and international reach, we have an extraordinary opportunity to elevate celiac disease in the public conversation. We want millions of people affected by this disease to feel seen and heard while building greater awareness of the urgent need for earlier diagnosis, better care, and treatments beyond the gluten-free diet."

The series will translate complex medical and scientific topics into accessible conversations while centering the lived experiences of patients and families. Planned episodes will explore the current state of celiac disease, the diagnostic journey, manifestations beyond the gastrointestinal system, pediatric care, gluten-free nutrition and labeling, follow-up care, mental health and quality of life, persistent symptoms, disease prediction and prevention, clinical trials, emerging therapies, and the future of celiac disease care.

"The science of celiac disease is advancing rapidly, but there remains a considerable gap between what researchers and clinicians are learning and what patients, families, and the wider public understand about the condition," said Dawn Adams, M.D., president of the Society for the Study of Celiac Disease. "Inside Celiac can help close that gap by bringing accurate, evidence-based information into engaging and relatable conversations."

Through Lowes' authentic and approachable hosting style, Inside Celiac will invite listeners into conversations that are informative, inspiring, and grounded in both scientific evidence and real-world experience. The podcast will also highlight the people driving progress across the celiac disease community, from researchers pursuing new diagnostics and therapies to advocates working to improve food safety, access to care, and quality of life.

Inside Celiac will premiere on Thursday October 15, 2026, with new episodes available on the third Thursday of each month. Listeners can find the series on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pandora, iHeart, YouTube, and all platforms where podcasts are hosted.

To learn more about Inside Celiac and receive updates when new episodes are released, visit www.celiac.org/insideceliac.

The Celiac Disease Foundation is the nation's leading patient advocacy organization for celiac disease. For more than three decades, the Foundation has worked to accelerate diagnosis, treatments, and a cure through research, education, and advocacy. The Foundation leads programs that connect patients with clinical trials, advance medical education, support patients and families, and elevate celiac disease as a public health priority. Katie Lowes is an acclaimed actress, director, producer, and podcast host known for her roles in the television series Scandal, Inventing Anna, and The Hunting Wives, as well as numerous film, television, theater, and voice performances. releases.body:
ALLENHURST, N.J., Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Commercial real estate brokerage firm Bielat Santore & Company has released Episode 7 of its Owner's Edge Podcast Series. The episode provides restaurant operators, license holders, developers, lenders, and municipal officials with an authoritative breakdown of New Jersey's major liquor license statutory overhauls.

New Jersey recently reformed its retail alcoholic beverage licensing framework twice within less than three years. These legislative updates ended the long-standing practice of indefinite dormancy for inactive "pocket" licenses, established structured activation timelines, and opened new intermunicipal transfer mechanisms designed to drive economic redevelopment.

Key Highlights Covered in Episode 7 (Part 2):

  • Ending Indefinite 12.39 Relief (P.L. 2023, c.290): Historically under N.J.S.A. 33:1-12.39, inactive Class C license holders could repeatedly petition the Director of the Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) for good-cause "12.39 relief" to maintain dormant licenses across consecutive terms.
  • The 2026 Reset & Revised Quartile Timetable (P.L. 2026, c.46): Enacted on July 23, 2026, P.L. 2026, c.46 superseded key portions of the 2024 law, resetting the four-group inactive license quartile schedule to run one, two, three, and four years from July 23, 2026.
  • Municipal Extensions & 30-Day ABC Appeals: Under the 2026 law, municipal issuing authorities possess expanded discretion to grant extensions beyond two consecutive inactive terms when a licensee demonstrates documented good-faith efforts to activate or transfer the license.
  • Three Distinct Intermunicipal Transfer Pathways: P.L. 2026, c.46 replaced the earlier contiguous municipality restrictions with three flexible transfer procedures to serve qualifying redevelopment, revitalization, or improvement areas[6]:
  1. Municipal Sale of a Newly Authorized License: Allows a municipality authorized to issue a new license to offer it at public sale to private bidders or to the highest bidding municipality statewide[14][15].

releases.body:
NEW YORK, Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Conversations around suicide and mental health are often brushed off in our culture, leaving many with feelings of isolation and helplessness and fears around being judged. The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP) addresses this head-on, launching a new season of its podcast channel where mental health experts and those with their own personal experiences related to mental health and suicide have honest, authentic, and open conversations, sharing insights from real people and communities, as well as the field's latest scientific developments and research.

Officially launched in December 2025, the AFSP Podcast Channel is entering its second season. In new episodes of Ask Dr. Jill, Strong Talk, and Elevating Voices, listeners can expect to learn about the latest research in the field, hear from changemakers who are reshaping mental healthcare, and have their real mental health and suicide-related questions answered by researchers, advocates, and licensed mental health professionals.

Season two's kickoff episodes in October:

  • Ask Dr. Jill, "What Can We Do to Prevent Physician Suicide?": Host Dr. Jill Harkavy-Friedman and Corey Feist, co-founder & CEO of the Dr. Lorna Breen Foundation, discuss the problem of physician suicide: the causes, the impact, and what we can do to prevent it
  • Strong Talk, next episode airing Oct. 21: Host Vic Armstrong has a candid conversation with Gemma Correll, bestselling author and graphic novelist (Anxietyland), known for integrating humor into their story of living with and navigating anxiety and depression

What's in store this season:

  • Dr. Lynnette A. Averill, a researcher specializing in psychedelics and their potential applications in mental health, on what research says about mental health and the use of psychedelics
  • Megan McCoy, CFT™, LMFT, and PhD, on the connection between personal finances and mental health – and how people can manage their emotions related to financial stress
  • Faye Seidler, LGBTQ+ suicide prevention advocate, on trans and LGBTQ+ suicide prevention and access to care in local communities
  • Vikram Patel, co-director of Harvard's Mental Health for All Lab, on what must be done to provide mental healthcare support care in low-resource settings
  • Dr. Ellie Foster, the co-director of Education for the Kevin Love Fund, on the role public figures and athletes play in empowering youth to explore vulnerability and have honest mental health conversations
  • Cultural considerations of mental health and suicide prevention in diverse communities

"We will be having conversations that combine real world experiences and research findings and offer our audience actionable content," said Dr. Jill Harkavy-Friedman, the host of Ask Dr. Jill and AFSP senior vice president of Research. "The new season invites listeners to meet and learn from interesting people who are changing the way we access mental health resources, making them more accessible to all," said Vic Armstrong, the host of Strong Talk and Elevating Voices and AFSP VP for Health Equity and Engagement.

The AFSP Podcast Channel houses the following shows:

Strong Talk is hosted by Vic Armstrong, AFSP's vice president for Health Equity and Engagement. Each episode features conversations with experts, advocates, and changemakers about how they're reshaping mental healthcare to make it accessible to all. The show covers topical issues that affect the mental health of various communities.

Elevating Voices is a roundtable discussion series where we bring together leaders from diverse communities to understand the unique mental health experiences they face and explore the ways we can all help to support and amplify progress.

Ask Dr. Jill features Dr. Jill Harkavy-Friedman, AFSP's senior vice president of Research, answering urgent and real mental health questions with the latest scientific research and conversations with fellow experts in the field.

Visit afsp.org/podcasts to learn more.

The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention is dedicated to saving lives and bringing hope to those affected by suicide, including those who have experienced a loss. AFSP creates a culture that's smart about mental health through public education and community programs, develops suicide prevention through research and advocacy, and provides support for those affected by suicide. Led by CEO Robert Gebbia and headquartered in New York, with its Policy and Advocacy Office in Washington, D.C., AFSP has local chapters in all 50 states, D.C., and Puerto Rico, with programs and events nationwide. Learn more about AFSP in its latest Annual Report and join the conversation on suicide prevention by following AFSP on Facebook, X, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and TikTok.

The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention and The Jed Foundation (JED) intend to merge as equals to form AFSP/JED, the nation's largest nonprofit dedicated to preventing suicide across the lifespan, and bringing hope to those affected by suicide loss or risk. The AFSP/JED mission would reflect a commitment to bring together AFSP's research, advocacy, chapter network, and loss-support expertise with JED's comprehensive approach to suicide prevention and evidence-informed youth mental health programs, creating greater scale, reach, and impact at a time of urgent national need. Read more about our recent announcement.

The news follows the show's national 2026 Best of the Year Award in Tech & Media, from a program created by former Hearst Magazines senior editors.

The Signal Awards are "mission-focused on uplifting the podcast medium by recognizing the most potent, meaningful and unprecedented audio projects being made today." Its judges – ranging from author Jay Shetty to content executives at Ted Talks, NPR and YouTube -- are described as "the architects, instigators and trailblazers of the medium."

The finalist episode, "Writing to Surprise Ourselves: Fire Survivor Kathleen Katims' Saved by a Story," is also in the running for the Signal Listener's Choice Award, a global public vote that drew more than 385,000 votes in 2025. Fans can vote through Oct. 15 at vote.signalaward.com. Gold, Silver and Bronze winners will be announced Oct. 20.

The recognition is remarkable given how the show began. Two weeks after the January 2025 "fire hurricane" devastated two Los Angeles communities, veteran podcast host Kim Marshall -- who escaped the Palisades Fire on foot with a small suitcase and two dogs -- launched #L.A. Rising with no network behind it, just a $5,000 small business grant from L.A. County Supervisor Lindsay Horvath's office and a pro bono production partner. Her goal: a trusted place for survivors' stories of resilience, and for expert resources and wellness tools, long after national media moved on.

"What stood out most to me was the raw authenticity: a survivor host sharing survivor stories, without the distance much disaster coverage carries," said one Best of the Year judge.

With Emmy-winning broadcaster Giselle Fernandez as Advising Producer, #L.A. Rising has expanded to disasters worldwide, from flooding in Brazil and Texas Hill Country to Category 5 Hurricane Melissa in Jamaica. Its premise: lessons learned from one disaster can be a catalyst of hope and inspiration for the next. Wellness Lift segments pair each story with coping strategies like deep breathing, contrast bathing, meditation and understanding grief.

International podcast agency NOVA helps produce the show. "This wasn't just a local story — it was a global moment," said NOVA CEO Hayden Lyon. "When Kim came to us with #L.A. Rising, launching it pro bono was an easy decision."

Since early 2026, Marshall and NOVA also help produce After the Fire USA's "How to Disaster" podcast on megafire recovery.

releases.body:
NOVATO, Calif., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Brayton Purcell LLP is highlighting a recent episode of Bloomberg's Big Take podcast, "Crafting America's Favorite Countertops Is Killing Workers," that brings national attention to the growing artificial stone silicosis crisis affecting artificial stone countertop fabrication workers across the United States.

The episode examines the fatal health risks associated with fabricating artificial stone countertops, a product that has become one of the nation's most popular countertop materials. Through the story of former countertop fabricator Tyler Jordan, Bloomberg explores the devastating impact of artificial stone silicosis, the litigation filed by affected artificial stone fabrication workers, and the ongoing debate regarding responsibility within the industry.

Artificial stone is at least 90% respirable crystalline silica, and the remaining approximately 10% consists of highly toxic dyes, resins, glues, and heavy metals. During fabrication activities such as cutting, grinding, polishing, and shaping slabs, enormous quantities of nano-sized, high-surface area toxic artificial stone dust is released into the air.

When inhaled, these particles penetrate deep into the lungs and become embedded in lung tissue. The resulting inflammation and scarring leads to artificial stone silicosis, a devastating, progressive, incurable, and fatal disease. Unlike many occupational diseases, artificial stone silicosis continues to progress long after exposure has ended.

According to Bloomberg labor reporter Josh Eidelson, artificial stone contains significantly higher levels of crystalline silica than natural stone products. During the podcast, he noted that artificial stone can contain approximately 93% crystalline silica, compared with substantially lower amounts in materials such as marble.

The Bloomberg episode focuses heavily on the experience of Tyler Jordan, who began working in his family's countertop fabrication business after graduating from high school. As artificial stone became an increasingly large part of the shop's work, he spent much of his time fabricating artificial stone slabs.

Jordan recalled that he was told artificial stone was stronger, less porous, and more resistant to staining than natural stone. However, according to the podcast, he and other workers were not warned that artificial stone presented significantly different health risks.

While still in his twenties, Jordan began experiencing severe health problems, including unexplained weight loss, chest pain, back pain, and other symptoms. Following extensive medical testing and a lung biopsy, he was diagnosed with artificial stone silicosis.

The consequences extended beyond lung disease. Jordan later developed autoimmune disease and kidney failure and ultimately received a kidney transplant from his father. His illness forced him to leave the industry and relocate his family.

His story reflects a troubling trend documented by physicians and researchers around the world. While silicosis has existed for centuries, countertop workers who fabricate artificial stone are increasingly being diagnosed at younger ages and experience more severe and rapidly progressing disease than has historically been associated with silica exposure.

Bloomberg reported that thousands of cases of artificial stone silicosis have been identified worldwide. In the United States, workers in their twenties, thirties, and forties have been diagnosed with artificial stone silicosis, raising concerns among physicians, researchers, and public health professionals.

The podcast also examines litigation brought by workers who allege that exposure to silica released during artificial stone fabrication caused artificial stone silicosis and other serious illnesses. Approximately 700 workers throughout the United States have filed lawsuits against companies involved in manufacturing and distribution of artificial stone slabs. Workers allege that artificial stone is an extraordinarily hazardous product, and that the risks associated with artificial stone fabrication were not adequately disclosed. Defendants have denied wrongdoing and continue to maintain that artificial stone can be fabricated safely.

At the same time, policymakers continue to debate how best to respond to the growing crisis. Proposed responses discussed during the podcast range from restrictions on artificial stone fabrication to legislation that would affect certain claims involving manufacturers.

"Bloomberg's reporting highlights the profound impact artificial stone silicosis can have on workers and their families. Many of the individuals being diagnosed are experiencing debilitating lung disease and serious complications at an age when they should be building careers and raising families. As awareness of this occupational disease continues to grow, it is important for affected workers to understand their legal rights and the options that may be available to them," said James Nevin, Partner at Brayton Purcell LLP.

The Bloomberg episode emphasizes that artificial stone silicosis affects far more than a worker's lungs. Careers are cut short, families face financial hardship, and workers confront serious medical complications that affect multiple organ systems and lead to premature death.

WASHINGTON, Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Paralyzed Veterans of America launches "Voices of PVA" – an audio-only podcast designed to inform, empower, and connect veterans and people living with spinal cord injuries or diseases (SCI/D), like MS and ALS, and those who support them. Having debuted on September 22 and on the heels of PVA's One of One campaign, the podcast serves as the definitive voice of PVA and life with SCI/D. Every episode brings listeners inside the healthcare battles, legislative wins, adaptive sports journeys, and more shaping the lives of those with disabilities. Hosted by U.S. Navy SEAL veteran/Paralympian and editor-in-chief of Paraplegic News and Sports 'N Spokes magazines Al Kovach, as well as PVA reporter Chad Stewart, each installment features guests with personal ties to paralysis — from veteran athletes and policy leaders to caregivers, renowned researchers, and more.

"The 'Voices of PVA' podcast is an extension of PVA's commitment to ensuring veterans with spinal cord injuries and diseases, like MS and ALS, not only have access to trusted information and meaningful stories, but also feel seen and heard," said Carl Blake, CEO of Paralyzed Veterans of America. "We're creating a space where lived experiences, expert insights, and advocacy intersect in a way that is deeply human, highly impactful, and one of a kind. While most outlets cover veteran or disability issues, our podcast, like PVA's important work, covers them both."

The first season of "Voices of PVA" will feature 24 episodes – complete with powerful, actionable content. Whether you're new to the SCI/D community, a longtime advocate, or know someone living with a disability, "Voices of PVA" offers practical insights and a deeper connection to the issues that matter, with new episodes dropping every other week.

"This podcast is something PVA has wanted for a long time, and now we finally have it," said Robert Thomas, a U.S. Army veteran and national president of PVA. "Some of the most important conversations in our community happen when people come together, and 'Voices of PVA' creates a space for these conversations to reach further."

Listeners can expect a dynamic mix of personal stories, expert interviews, policy discussions, and practical guidance delivered in a format that is accessible, engaging, and rooted in real-world experience. The podcast represents a significant step forward in PVA's ongoing efforts to innovate how it connects with its community and elevates issues impacting veterans and people with disabilities.

"Conversations have power. A magazine article can inform you, but a conversation lets you hear someone's heart," Kovach said. "We hope every listener walks away from our podcast having learned something useful, felt inspired, and more connected to the community. If someone hears an episode and thinks, 'I'm not alone,' or 'I didn't know that resource existed' — that's success in our eyes."

Just two days following its launch, listeners flooded PVA with reactions, such as:

"The 'Voices of PVA' podcast creates a safe, engaging space for diverse perspectives to ask questions, sharpen our knowledge, and pass that knowledge along to our own communities," said Chadwick W., U.S. Air Force veteran and PVA Buckeye Chapter member. "[These] honest conversation[s], help to problem-solve better approaches to care and advocate to the broader community."

To learn more about the "Voices of PVA" podcast and its hosts visit PVA.org/VoicesOfPVA. To subscribe, leave a review, or share an episode with someone you know, visit Substack.com/@PVA1946.

About Paralyzed Veterans of America

Paralyzed Veterans of America is a 501(c)(3) non-profit and the only congressionally chartered veterans service organization dedicated solely for the benefit and representation of veterans with spinal cord injury or diseases. The organization ensures veterans receive the benefits earned through service to our nation; monitors their care in VA spinal cord injury units; and funds research and education in the search for a cure and improved care for individuals with paralysis.

As a life-long partner and advocate for veterans and all people with disabilities, PVA also develops training and career services, works to ensure accessibility in public buildings and spaces, and provides health and rehabilitation opportunities through sports and recreation. With more than 70 offices and 33 chapters, Paralyzed Veterans of America serves veterans, their families, and their caregivers in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. The Fibre Files gives us the opportunity to look beyond the technology and hear directly from people about how digital connectivity can impact communities, businesses, and individuals," said Sam Laprade, host of The Fibre Files.

Speaking with Jeff Kone on The Wall Street Resource, Mr. Halabu outlined how Z Squared acquires existing powered sites - former crypto mining and manufacturing facilities - and retrofits them for AI and high-performance computing use. He described the Company's role as a triple-net landlord, positioned the Union County Campus in Arkansas as its flagship asset, and reiterated the two measures he has asked shareholders to hold the Company to over the next 12 to 18 months: megawatts under management and signed leases.

Speaking with Will Tjernlund on The Nano Cap Podcast, Mr. Halabu traced his background in trading and real estate and the Company's path to the public markets, and detailed the criteria Z Squared applies to a prospective site - price, power and time to power, redundant fiber, water, and county and municipal support. He also addressed the expanding role of behind-the-meter generation as utility interconnection timelines lengthen, and why he expects land and power to remain scarce as AI compute demand grows.

"These conversations were a chance to be direct about what we are building and how it generates revenue," said David Halabu, Chief Executive Officer of Z Squared. Both interviews touched on the Company's previously announced acquisition of Paradox Data, LLC and the Union County Campus it brought with it. Set out below are the questions investors have most frequently raised about that transaction.

What did Z Squared acquire?

Z Squared acquired 100% of the membership interests of Paradox Data, LLC, whose flagship asset is the Union County Campus in El Dorado, Arkansas. The transaction closed on an all-stock basis - no cash at closing and no debt financing.

How much power does the Union County Campus have today, and how does it scale?

The campus has an existing arrangement with Entergy Arkansas for energy service of up to 8.0 MW, plus an executed contract for adjacent land. On The Wall Street Resource, Mr. Halabu described roughly eight megawatts of total capacity and six megawatts of critical capacity available today. The development pathway targets up to 150 MW over time through a combination of utility power and on-site generation, added in phases as utility timelines and customer demand allow.

How does Z Squared expect to generate revenue from the campus?

Z Squared intends to operate as a triple-net landlord, not a compute provider: it expects to lease the land, the building and access to power to tenants - primarily "neocloud" and enterprise AI users - with power treated as a pass-through, and does not intend to buy or lease GPUs. Mr. Halabu said he is hopeful the first six to eight megawatts can be monetized in the early-to-mid 2027 timeframe, subject to the factors described under "Forward-Looking Statements" below.

releases.body:
Segal Board Chair David Blumenstein Examines the Changing Benefits Landscape, the Enduring Value of Pensions and the Future of Retirement

WASHINGTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Institute on Retirement Security (NIRS) today released Episode 5 of its Retirement in America podcast, "The New Reality of Retirement and Workplace Benefits."

The new episode features David Blumenstein, board chair and immediate past president and CEO of Segal, and podcast host Dan Doonan in a wide-ranging conversation about the forces reshaping employee benefits and retirement security. They examine rising healthcare costs, the shift of retirement responsibility to individuals, the continuing value of pensions, changing expectations for workplace benefits, and how technology and artificial intelligence could transform the field.

Retirement in America is available on the NIRS website, YouTube, and all major podcast platforms.

"Healthcare and retirement benefits do not exist in separate silos," Doonan said. "When healthcare costs consume a larger share of compensation, there is less room for wages and retirement contributions. David brings decades of experience working with employers and plan sponsors, and this conversation helps explain why strengthening retirement security requires looking at the entire benefits landscape."

Blumenstein says the pace of change confronting employers and plan sponsors has accelerated significantly. On the retirement side, advances in computing have enabled more sophisticated risk modeling. On the healthcare side, employers are navigating rapidly evolving treatments, telehealth and other new approaches to care. At the same time, workers increasingly expect benefits information and tools to be as immediate and easy to use as other digital services.

The conversation also explores the broader shift toward placing more responsibility for saving for retirement on individual workers. Blumenstein says that while defined contribution plans are an important part of the retirement system, many workers cannot simply save more when their income is already consumed by basic necessities. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss the role defined benefit pensions can play by providing lifetime income workers can count on, as well as the need for personal savings to supplement retirement income.

Blumenstein also offers an optimistic view of technology and artificial intelligence. He expects new tools to make benefits analysis faster and more responsive while allowing employers and workers to model decisions more easily. But he emphasizes that critical thinking, problem solving and judgment will remain essential as the benefits field continues to evolve.

Among the topics discussed in the episode:

  • Rising healthcare costs and retirement security. Healthcare inflation puts pressure on employer compensation budgets, potentially leaving less available for wages and retirement benefits while workers and retirees face higher medical expenses.
  • The changing employee benefits landscape. Employers and plan sponsors are adapting to faster technological change, new healthcare treatments and rising expectations for easy, real-time access to benefits information.
  • The growing burden on individuals. Workers are increasingly responsible for saving for their own retirement, even as affordability pressures can make it difficult to maximize 401(k) or IRA contributions.
  • The enduring value of pensions. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss how defined benefit plans provide lifetime income and reduce some of the complex financial decisions and risks individuals otherwise must manage on their own.
  • Technology and AI. Blumenstein sees technology as a force that can improve modeling, communication and decision-making, while increasing the importance of critical thinking and problem solving.
  • A collective approach to retirement security. The episode closes with a discussion of the need for employers, policymakers and other stakeholders to work together on challenges that cannot be solved by individuals alone.

Retirement in America is a podcast from NIRS examining the economic, workforce and policy trends influencing retirement security. Combining expert insight with real-world experiences, the podcast helps listeners better understand one of the most important financial issues facing American workers and families today.

The National Institute on Retirement Security is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization established to contribute to informed policymaking by fostering a deep understanding of the value of retirement security to employees, employers, and the economy as a whole. Located in Washington, D.C., NIRS membership includes financial services firms, employee benefit plans, trade associations, and other retirement service providers.

Hosted by award-winning filmmaker and environmental journalist Aliya Jasmine, the second season premieres Sept. 17.

TORONTO, Sept. 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- WWF-Canada's top science podcast This Is Wild returns for a second season, opening with a powerful episode about the urgent threats facing southern resident killer whales, one of Canada's most iconic species.

The season premiere revisits the story of Tahlequah, the southern resident killer whale who captured international attention in 2018 when she carried her dead calf through the Salish Sea for 17 days (a behaviour we saw again in 2025 after the tragic loss of another calf). Her journey became a symbol of this orca population in crisis and raised awareness about the immense pressures they're facing.

Declining chinook salmon populations, underwater noise from vessels and industry, and pollution are just some of the growing threats to southern resident killer whales. Today, only around 75 remain, with their future hanging in a precarious balance.

Episode 1 features WWF-Canada conservation experts Hussein Alidina and Emily Giles alongside Ecojustice lawyer Margot Venton with narration by award-winning environmental journalist Aliya Jasmine. Together they explore the science behind these threats, the conservation efforts aimed at supporting their recovery, and the legal and policy hurdles that are slowing down action and ramping up risks.

"We know better. We have to do better. It's our responsibility to do better. And we need to do that better because in many ways, we're part of the same circle of life that the whales are," said Hussein Alidina, WWF-Canada's lead specialist for marine conservation.

"Southern resident killer whales are one of the most beloved species in Canada, and one of the most endangered. At a time when Canada is accelerating approvals for major projects like ports and pipelines that risk their survival, the first episode of This is Wild asks the important question of what we're willing to lose for economic gain," said Megan Leslie, WWF-Canada's president and CEO. "Each episode takes listeners to different parts of the country, exploring the species that are shaping our world and what it will take to protect theirs."

Co-produced with Antica Productions, the second season of This Is Wild continues WWF-Canada's commitment to making conservation stories engaging and accessible.

Aliya Jasmine previously appeared on an episode of WWF-Canada's Good Nature podcast, talking about her new short documentary Bird Names.

ALLENHURST, N.J. , Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Commercial real estate brokerage firm Bielat Santore & Company has officially released Episode 6 (Part I) of its Owner's Edge Podcast Series, titled "New Jersey Liquor Licenses: Regulatory Structure and Market Value". The episode delivers a comprehensive analysis of how New Jersey's unique statutory framework governs retail alcoholic beverage licenses and creates private-market economic value.

Although New Jersey law classifies a liquor license as a regulated government privilege rather than ordinary property, eligible licenses command substantial market value across the state.

Key Topics Covered in Episode 6 (Part I):

  • The Statutory Framework & Municipal Population Caps: Established under Title 33 following the repeal of Prohibition in 1933, New Jersey's Alcoholic Beverage Control system ties retail licenses to local population limits.
  • Essential Class C Retail Licenses: An overview of key retail license types, including Type 33 (Plenary Retail Consumption for standard bar/restaurant service), Type 32 (Plenary Retail Consumption with Broad Package Privilege, no longer newly issued), Type 44 (Plenary Retail Distribution for package stores).
  • Person-to-Person & Place-to-Place Transfers: Clarifying the legal separation between purchasing a business asset and transferring a license.
  • The Six-Step Valuation Framework: Addressing why there is no standardized statewide price database and presenting a six-step valuation methodology.

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The transition to clean energy is no longer constrained by technology—it is purely a matter of execution.

The Planet Classroom Network, in partnership with VoiceAmerica, today announces the podcast release of Net Zero Speaks to Andrew Blakers. Hosted by youth climate advocate Ivan Ransom, this briefing features Professor Andrew Blakers AO FAA FTSE FRSN of the Australian National University, one of the world's leading renewable energy researchers and co-developer of the PERC solar cell technology used in much of today's global solar industry.

At the heart of the discussion is an unequivocal message: the world already possesses the technology required to run on 100 percent renewable energy.

"We have everything we need," Blakers explains. "We don't need to invent anything. It's just a matter of getting out and doing it."

A VISION FOR CHEAP, CLEAN ENERGY FOREVER

Throughout the conversation, Blakers outlines a global future powered by what he calls "clean, cheap energy forever," noting that "most countries are their own Saudi Arabia of solar and wind."

Drawing on decades of research, he demonstrates how solar power, wind energy, pumped hydro storage, batteries, and electrification technologies can seamlessly integrate to create reliable, affordable, zero-carbon energy systems at scale worldwide.

A GLOBAL VOICE ON RENEWABLE INNOVATION

Professor Blakers is internationally recognized for helping develop the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell (PERC) solar cell—a breakthrough that dramatically increased solar panel efficiency, transformed the modern solar industry, and accelerated the dramatic decline in solar energy costs globally.

Today, Blakers leads research on large-scale renewable energy systems and the Global Pumped Hydro Atlas, which identifies hundreds of thousands of potential energy storage sites capable of supporting fully renewable electricity grids.

Key insights highlighted in the episode include:

  • The Scale of Solar & Wind: Why most nations possess more than enough renewable resources to achieve total energy independence.
  • Overcoming Misconceptions: Tackling persistent myths regarding land use, raw materials, grid stability, and waste management.
  • Deep Decarbonization: How governments, utilities, and communities can achieve deep decarbonization while maintaining lower energy costs and grid reliability.

FROM SOLAR PANELS TO "GRAVITY BATTERIES"

A central focus of the episode is solving the energy storage puzzle. Blakers explains how pumped hydro systems—often described as giant "gravity batteries"—store renewable energy by moving water between two reservoirs at different elevations.

His team's research identified approximately 820,000 potential pumped hydro sites globally, offering vastly more storage capacity than needed for a fully renewable energy future. The discussion explores how these systems balance solar and wind generation while maintaining grid reliability and affordability.

"Professor Blakers reminds us that many of the critical solutions we need already exist," said C. M. (Cathy) Rubin, Co-Founder and CEO of Planet Classroom. "Understanding that we already have the tools to solve these challenges is empowering for young people. The challenge now is accelerating action and building the political and social will to implement them globally."

releases.title: Your Muscles May Be One of Your Most Valuable Retirement Assets
releases.body:
Fitness & Finance co-founders explain why preserving muscle should be part of the retirement-planning conversation

FREDERICKSBURG, Va., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- When it comes to retirement planning, most people focus on how much to save and where to invest it. But another asset can have an enormous influence on how those retirement years are lived: muscle. Maintaining strength and muscle mass as we age can help support mobility, balance and independence—factors that can influence both quality of life and healthcare needs later in life. The good news is that it is never too late to start investing in physical strength.

"We spend decades building a financial portfolio for retirement, but we should be building our physical portfolio at the same time," said Jennifer Scherer, co-founder of the Fitness & Finance Radio podcast, registered dietitian, medical exercise specialist, certified personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of Fredericksburg Fitness Studio. "Muscle is one of the assets that helps protect our ability to move, remain independent and enjoy the life we worked so hard to build. Financial longevity means much less if our physical health doesn't allow us to enjoy it."

While people are focused on building their financial portfolio, they may be overlooking their physical one. Age-related losses in muscle and strength can affect mobility, balance and independence and are associated with greater risk of falls and hospitalization. Those health consequences can also create significant expenses during retirement.

According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), starting at around 30, our bodies naturally begin losing muscle mass. We lose 3-5% of muscle mass every decade, and while that change may happen slowly, it adds up, leaving people with weakened strength. Sarcopenia, the gradual loss of muscle mass, increases the risks of falls, broken bones, and hospitalization. These are all things that are going to dip into the financial savings that someone has accumulated for retirement.

A study published in the Journal of Frailty & Aging reports that the hospitalization costs associated with sarcopenia are around $40 billion. They report that those with the condition are more likely to be hospitalized, with it costing each person an average of over $2,300 per year. Add to that the costs that people incur outside of the hospital due to broken bones, falls, and any hired help they need due to the lack of independence. It adds up to a financial burden that people may have been able to avoid if they had worked on maintaining muscle mass over the years.

The key is to start working on building and maintaining muscle mass, regardless of what age someone is at. It's never too late to take this issue on. According to the NIH, 30% of adults over the age of 70 have trouble walking, getting up from a chair, or climbing stairs. They report that such mobility issues not only lead to a loss of independence, but are also linked to higher rates of falls, chronic diseases, nursing home admissions, and mortality. They report that the big culprit is a loss of muscle mass, and that it can be slowed down by maintaining an active lifestyle.

Here are some tips to keep in mind to help slow the muscle-mass loss problem:

  • Get active no matter what age you are. Know that you can always start slow and build it up as you get stronger. Being physically active is crucial to healthier aging.
  • Ensure that your workout routine has you lifting weights and challenging yourself. It's important to get things in there like resistance exercises. Include progressive resistance training. Muscles need an appropriate challenge to adapt and remain strong. Resistance can come from weights, machines, bands or body weight, and the program should be appropriate for the individual's health, abilities and experience.
  • Be sure to get the right foods in your diet in order to build and maintain muscle. Getting enough protein is a must in order to build and maintain muscle mass over the years. Know how much you need per day and pay attention to ensure you get it. Prioritize adequate nutrition, particularly protein. Protein provides the amino acids needed to support muscle maintenance and repair, but individual needs vary based on age, health status and activity level.
  • If you have one day that you slip or one week where you falter on your new fitness plans, don't give up. Just start again. Too often, people throw in the towel and give up, rather than simply getting back at it. Working with someone, such as a coach or trainer, can help keep you on track.
  • Build a professional team. A qualified fitness or healthcare professional can assess physical function and help create an appropriate plan for maintaining strength and mobility, while a qualified financial professional can help prepare for the financial realities of retirement. Both plans should support the same goal: maintaining independence and quality of life for as long as possible.

"One of the biggest expenses in retirement can be needing help with the things you once did independently," said Jeff Smith, co-founder of Fitness & Finance Radio, financial planning expert, personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of The Retirement Smith. "We can build a strong financial plan, but preserving the physical ability to enjoy those years is equally important. Financial planning and fitness planning have more in common than people realize: both benefit from starting early, being consistent and thinking long-term."

Smith and Scherer co-founded Fitness & Finance Radio to explore an often-overlooked connection: the relationship between physical health and financial health throughout the lifespan. Drawing on Scherer's expertise in nutrition, medical exercise and fitness and Smith and Scherer are a married couple who co-founded the Fitness & Finance Radio podcast, where they come together to share their fields of expertise. The information focuses on offering a mix of nutrition, healthy lifestyle, and financial retirement planning strategies. Listeners can tune in to hear the duo discuss the issues and gain advice and insight that may help them now and in their retirement years. The Fitness & Finance Radio podcast is available for free on YouTube. Recent episode topics cover credibility, stress, funding adult children, saving money and losing weight on vacation, obesity and preventative care, and more. To get more information and listen, visit the site at: https://www.youtube.com/@fitnessfinanceradio?app=desktop

Fitness & Finance Radio is a podcast produced by the married couple Jeff Smith and Jennifer Scherer. Scherer is a registered dietitian, fitness expert, and founder of Fredericksburg Fitness Studio.
